title: Show HN: Luciole Mono – terminal font designed for legibility
content:
Comments
TLDR : Atkinson Hyperlegible Mono alternative

Luciole Mono is a vibe-clauded derivative of Luciole.Luciole was designed for visually impaired readers by Laurent Bourcellier and Jonathan Perez, at the Centre Technique Régional pour la Déficience Visuelle (typographies.fr)

Please tell me what you think - thanks in advance

thehamkercat · Nov 28, 2026

Does this really look more readable than Jetbrains Mono nerd-font?

smallerize · Nov 28, 2026

No, but it was hard for me to explain why it's worse than the original Luciole. Usually for "readability" I start by looking for really open counters, which it doesn't have. I think it relies more on "word shape", and depends on a very regular pattern of vertical lines. Converting this to mono is not possible, especially the really tight spacing on the i and l characters.

I think it was an interesting experiment, and hopefully OP learned that fonts are more than just letter shapes.

amoshebb · Nov 28, 2026

As "Luciole Mono" it works great, although frankly I'm unsure I like the bottom-heavy 'r' (it's almost jarring in double r words like, well, jarring).

As "Completing the Luciole Superfamily" where it has great math coverage, I think it fails. Luciole is great because it has such a high-contrast bold and (for a sans serif) italic.

If I'm giving a presentation and want to include one `keyword` or code snippet, I'm sometimes inlining it and actually want a fairly jarring 'typewriter' font which looks intentionally very monospace.

I usually end up reaching for bolded Courier Prime for that reason, but it's odd in other ways. I would love to see a "typewriter" variant of this mono font which is, somehow, obviously different while feeling like it belongs / following the broad letterforms.

Octoth0rpe · Nov 28, 2026

I'm a bit of a monospace font snob and I like this quite a bit. A couple of observations:

- in the example text, the `{i}` and `[l]` look quite odd to me. The bottom of the braces fall below the baseline, but the tops don't extend as far above the characters proportionally (especially noticeable on the l).

- Looks a _little_ to thick for my tastes, but maybe a light variant would help. The thickness particularly hurts the lowercase r.

- kerning looks a little rough in some uppercase combinations, see `GH`, `MN`, `CD` (I only checked the standard alphabet ordering, not a list of known problematic combinations.

- rough lowerspace combinations: `fg`, `jk` look a little too far apart

Not OP. For monospace, I like Source Code Pro[1], because it has distict letterforms (1 v.s. l, etc.), decent glyph coverage, and a full set of variants (light, italic, bold, etc.).
